title: Gideon and the Lantern
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Vessany, Xanthe Thornbury works as a courier carrying sealed diplomatic codes between a collapsing government and its last allies, hiding in plain sight among refugees. When a census taker named Gideon Hale asks one question too many, Xanthe's cover shatters — but Gideon, it turns out, is keeping secrets of his own, including a forged lantern-pass that grants one person safe passage out before the armistice seals the borders. As Xanthe ferries the final code that could either delay or doom the surrender, they must decide who receives the last berth: their ailing mother, their young brother, or the stranger who has become something more. In the end, Xanthe gives the berth away, stays behind to deliver the code that buys the city an evacuation corridor instead of a single escape — and finds that belonging was never a place you fled to, but the people you refused to abandon.
about_author: Mara Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from displaced families of vanished states. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of endings.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Paper
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet them threading through occupied Vessany with diplomatic codes sewn into a coat lining, hands busy, face forgettable. A small errand for their mother's medicine establishes family stakes. Emotional beat: controlled anonymity as survival, and the first tremor of fear that the republic's last days are numbered.

chapters.title: Questions on the Census Form
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The census taker works his rounds methodically, noting who is home, who has fled, who lies. He knocks at the Thornbury door and asks about household members born outside the district — a question not on any official form. Emotional beat: quiet menace; Gideon is not what his badge says he is.

chapters.title: A Lie Told Well
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe deflects Gideon's questions with practiced ease, but he notices the ink stains on their fingers matching courier dispatch ink. He leaves without arresting anyone — and leaves a chalk mark on the doorframe. Emotional beat: the sick recognition of being seen after years of being invisible.

chapters.title: The Lantern in the Window
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Alone in his office, Gideon reveals his secret: a genuine evacuation berth certificate hidden inside a defunct lighthouse lantern, payment for a debt he can never repay honestly. He watches the Thornbury window across the square. Emotional beat: guilt and longing; the watcher is himself trapped.

chapters.title: Mother's Cough
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Their mother's illness worsens as coal rations vanish; brother Tam hoards scrap metal to barter. Xanthe delivers a code that orders the navy to scuttle its own fleet and realizes the armistice terms are already written. Emotional beat: grief arriving early, mourning a country still technically alive.

chapters.title: The Chalk Mark
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam discovers the chalk mark and scrubs it off, then follows Gideon through the market, convinced he's an informer. Instead he witnesses Gideon bribing a dock clerk. Emotional beat: adolescent fury curdling into confusion — the enemy may be buying passage, not selling names.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Summoned to a ministry basement, Xanthe is questioned by their own handler about the census taker's interest in them. The handler suspects Gideon is a foreign agent hunting the final code. Emotional beat: paranoia from every direction; duty tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Two Liars at a Bread Line
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Xanthe confronts Gideon in the bread queue; each accuses the other of espionage until mutual exhaustion strips the performances away. They share bread and, cautiously, truths. Emotional beat: the first honest conversation either has had in years — connection born of shared deception.

chapters.title: What the Lantern Holds
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon shows Xanthe the berth certificate hidden in the lantern, confessing he took this posting to place it in worthy hands. Xanthe thinks immediately of their mother. Emotional beat: unbearable hope — one life can be saved, which means choosing whose.

chapters.title: The Code That Could Delay It
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe learns the final dispatch they carry contains a clause that could stall the armistice long enough to open an evacuation corridor for thousands — if delivered to the right signatory before the signing. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of one berth versus one corridor.

chapters.title: Tam Runs
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, believing he can trade information about the code for three berths, approaches the occupying liaison office and barely escapes being detained. Gideon covers his flight at personal risk. Emotional beat: love expressed recklessly; the family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Handler's Offer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The handler offers Xanthe immunity and two berths in exchange for delivering the code to him instead — he intends to bury the delay clause and sign quickly, protecting his own family. Emotional beat: corruption wearing a familiar face; duty revealed as self-interest at the top.

chapters.title: Night at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Xanthe and Gideon shelter in the decommissioned lighthouse during an artillery barrage, the lantern lit between them. They speak of the people they were before the war and almost touch. Emotional beat: tenderness as defiance; love admitted in the space between explosions.

chapters.title: Mother Knows
chapters.summary: Mother's POV (rare interlude). Bedridden, Mother has understood everything for weeks. She quietly tells Xanthe she will not take the berth — that her life is spent, and theirs is not. Emotional beat: maternal love as the story's moral center; the choice reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Betrayal at the Ministry
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe delivers the code to the handler, who burns the delay clause in front of them — but Xanthe memorized it years of courier work ago. They walk out knowing they now carry the only copy in their head. Emotional beat: cold fury transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Snow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the armistice hours away, both the handler's men and the occupiers hunt Xanthe. Gideon uses his census records to build them a false identity trail through the city. Emotional beat: pursuit and partnership; trust proven under fire.

chapters.title: The Signing Room
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe infiltrates the armistice signing as a document courier and recites the delay clause to the one signatory who might honor it — an old adversary of the handler. The room holds its breath. Emotional beat: climax; one voice against the machinery of surrender.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The clause passes: the armistice is delayed two days, and the evacuation corridor opens. Boats fill; the handler is arrested by his own ministry. But there is only time for one more berth decision. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by cost; no clean wins.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the dock, Xanthe puts Tam on the boat with the berth, pressing Mother's ring into his hand. Gideon chooses to stay, tearing up his own exit papers. Emotional beat: heartbreak and certainty entwined; letting go as the truest form of keeping.

chapters.title: What the Corridor Carried
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, writing from across the water. Tam describes the crossing and the strangers aboard who owe their lives to a clause one courier refused to let die. Emotional beat: witness and gratitude; the meaning of the sacrifice made visible from afar.

chapters.title: Ashes and Addresses
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The city falls quietly. Xanthe and Gideon remain among those who stayed, helping register the displaced — Gideon with his census lists, Xanthe with codes now used to reunite families instead of move armies. Emotional beat: grief metabolized into purpose; belonging rebuilt from ruins.

chapters.title: The Lantern Rekindled
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epilogue. Spring comes. In the relit lighthouse, Xanthe and Gideon keep the lantern burning as a beacon for boats still finding the corridor, and a letter arrives from Tam. Emotional beat: resolution — memory kept alight, love chosen over escape, home redefined as the people who stayed.
